neighbours.label: the slot right after a verb of releasing or depositing something from oneself (lay/deposit their eggs, let out a sound, leave you with a thought)
fire: Every spring the sea turtles return to deposit their eggs on the beach.
Many insects lay their eggs on the underside of leaves.
The salmon swim upstream to spawn and lay their eggs in gravel.
Before we finish, I would like to leave you with a short story.
The crowd let out a loud cheer when the goal went in.
Female mosquitoes lay their eggs in standing water.
The old man let out a deep laugh at the joke.
Hens in our yard lay their eggs in the straw box.
quiet: Every spring the sea turtles return to feed along the beach.
Many insects hide from birds on the underside of leaves.
The salmon swim upstream each autumn and rest in the gravel.
Before we finish, I would like to thank everyone for coming.
The crowd stood up quickly when the goal went in.
Female mosquitoes look for blood near standing water.
The old man smiled warmly at the joke.
Hens in our yard sleep at night in the straw box.

notes: Probe: 'lay their eggs' strong (0.67), 'let out' moderate, 'drop off' weak. Opposite pole is about holding back what one wants to say.
